anchor: on all four demand signals, at five bin resolutions, under one rolling-origin protocol
claim_text: Evaluation covers four demand signals (requests, images, context tokens, generated tokens) at five bin resolutions (1s, 15s, 30s, 45s, 1min) with rolling-origin protocol

anchor: Origins advance in strides of $H$, every origin a multiple of $H$: consecutive forecasts tile the timeline into a continuous, non-overlapping prediction path
claim_text: Rolling origins advance in strides of H=12 bins, tiling timeline into continuous non-overlapping prediction path

anchor: TimesFM has no covariate interface and is the strict univariate-per-signal control
claim_text: TimesFM lacks covariate interface, serves as univariate-only control

anchor: Chronos-2 forecasts each target with the other three series supplied as past-only covariates, its native conditioning path; Toto-2 forecasts all four signals jointly as one multivariate series
claim_text: Chronos-2 uses other three series as past-only covariates; Toto-2 forecasts all four jointly as multivariate series

anchor: Point forecasts are the median for Chronos-2 and Toto-2, the mean head for TimesFM, and the model value for the baselines, whose quantile bands are Gaussian prediction intervals
claim_text: Point forecasts: median for Chronos-2/Toto-2, mean head for TimesFM, model value for baselines; baseline quantiles are Gaussian prediction intervals

anchor: All forecasts are floored at zero (rates are non-negative)
claim_text: All forecasts floored at zero due to non-negative rates

anchor: The nine quantile levels $0.1, \ldots, 0.9$ are the intersection of the three models' native heads
claim_text: Nine quantile levels (0.1 to 0.9) used, intersection of models' native quantile heads

anchor: Accuracy is reported as WAPE, $\sum_t |\hat y_t - y_t| \,/ \sum_t y_t$ (scale-free and defined on zero-signal bins), alongside MAE where absolute units aid interpretation
claim_text: Metrics: WAPE (scale-free, defined on zero bins) and MAE

anchor: comfortably inside any 15--60-second cadence
claim_text: Forecast latency (4-51ms) fits within 15-60 second decision cadence

anchor: a foundation-model forecaster is a GPU-resident 120M--2.5B-parameter service, EWMA a few lines of arithmetic
claim_text: Foundation models are GPU-resident 120M-2.5B parameter services; EWMA is few lines of arithmetic
Naive baseline WAPE: 1min - req 42.3%, img 67.8%, ctx 55.4%, gen 51.0%; 1s - req 82.0%, img 156.9%, ctx 124.6%, gen 119.9%
EWMA baseline WAPE: 1min - req 35.2%, img 54.2%, ctx 44.7%, gen 41.2%; 1s - req 68.1%, img 146.1%, ctx 106.0%, gen 100.0%
Holt-Winters baseline WAPE: 1min - req 43.8%, img 69.4%, ctx 56.4%, gen 53.5%; 1s - req 93.9%, img 217.0%, ctx 151.5%, gen 143.7%

anchor: the foundation models beat every baseline in all twenty cells, zero-shot, with no per-series tuning
claim_text: Foundation models beat all baselines in all 20 (resolution, signal) cells zero-shot without per-series tuning

anchor: always predicting zero scores exactly 100\%, so at 1-second bins the models move from far-worse-than-zero (the baselines) to par-with-zero, the white shot-noise floor
claim_text: Zero forecast yields 100% WAPE; at 1s bins baselines >100% (worse than zero), foundation models ~100% (par with zero)

anchor: which model wins is resolution-dependent, and the inter-model ranking is noise-level
claim_text: Model ranking depends on resolution; inter-model differences are noise-level

anchor: Toto-2 (usually with covariates) takes the fine-bin cells and Chronos-2 most of the coarse ones
claim_text: Toto-2 (often with covariates) wins fine bins; Chronos-2 wins coarse bins

anchor: But the spreads are small (typically under 2 WAPE points) and several bolded column wins are decided by $\leq$0.1 WAPE point, below plausible sampling variability with no significance test attached
claim_text: Inter-model spreads typically <2 WAPE points; some wins decided by ≤0.1 WAPE point, below sampling variability

anchor: Dynamo's SLA planner selects a load predictor from a fixed registry (ARIMA, Kalman, Prophet, or constant)
claim_text: Dynamo's SLA planner uses predictor registry: ARIMA, Kalman, Prophet, constant

anchor: Run through the same protocol on the image signal (shipped defaults; the constant predictor reproduces the naive baseline's WAPE exactly), all four sit at or below the classical frontier and none reaches the foundation-model level
claim_text: Dynamo's four predictors (ARIMA, Kalman, Prophet, constant) at shipped defaults all at/below classical frontier, none reach foundation model level on image signal
Chronos-2 covariate MAE change: 1min +0.16%, 45s +0.30%, 30s +0.34%, 15s -0.15%, 1s -0.39%

anchor: Context tokens are materially image-driven ($R^2 = 0.94$ regressing realized context on requests and images)
claim_text: Context tokens regressed on requests+images yields R²=0.94

anchor: pooled, the additive reconstruction ties or slightly trails the direct forecast, with no robust edge at the onsets
claim_text: Additive reconstruction (text + image forecast × token factor) ties or slightly trails direct forecast, no edge at onsets

anchor: TimesFM's mean head is beaten in nearly all its cells by the median or a lower quantile, and the Gaussian-band baselines account for most of the rest
claim_text: TimesFM mean head beaten by median/lower quantile in nearly all cells; Gaussian-band baselines account for rest

anchor: At provisioning cadences (15-second and 1-minute bins) the upper edge, the one provisioning consumes, is essentially calibrated for every model and signal: p90 coverage 0.88--0.90 against the nominal 0.90
claim_text: At 15s and 1min bins, p90 coverage 0.88-0.90 vs nominal 0.90 for all models/signals

anchor: Median coverage sits near 0.45; the lower edge is distorted by zero-ties (the p10 frequently touches zero on bursty signals), which also deflates the nominal-80\% band, more so at finer bins
claim_text: Median coverage ~0.45; lower edge distorted by zero-ties (p10 often zero), deflates 80% band, worse at finer bins

anchor: upper-quantile headroom is trustworthy at provisioning cadence; band-width and lower-edge semantics are not
claim_text: Upper quantile headroom trustworthy at provisioning cadence; band-width and lower-edge semantics not

anchor: Individual bins pierce the p90 edge near the nominal rate (11\% of common-span image bins)
claim_text: 11% of common-span image bins pierce p90 edge (near nominal 10%)

anchor: At the burst's collapse the stitched path lags by up to one horizon (12 minutes)
claim_text: At burst collapse, stitched forecast lags up to 12 minutes (one horizon)

anchor: Chronos-2 and Toto-2 postdate the trace's 2025 public release, so their pretraining corpora could in principle contain series derived from it
claim_text: Chronos-2 and Toto-2 postdate trace's 2025 release; pretraining may contain trace-derived series
expected_backing: model release dates vs trace release date

anchor: Chronos-2 occasionally emits locally crossed quantiles (its head does not enforce monotonicity); values are recorded as produced apart from the nonnegativity floor
claim_text: Chronos-2 occasionally emits crossed quantiles (no monotonicity enforcement); recorded as-produced except nonnegativity floor

anchor: Finally, results derive from one seven-day trace of one production cluster, with its by-construction 50/50 modality split
claim_text: Results from single 7-day trace of one production cluster with 50/50 modality split

anchor: The p90 band edge is empirically calibrated at provisioning cadence (coverage 0.88--0.90), making upper-quantile headroom a sound provisioning input
claim_text: p90 band edge calibrated at provisioning cadence (coverage 0.88-0.90), making upper-quantile headroom sound provisioning input

anchor: covariates are nearly irrelevant there, and for median-point models no fixed quantile improves on the point path --- the band is headroom, not correction
claim_text: Covariates nearly irrelevant at provisioning cadence; for median-point models no quantile improves point path; band is headroom not correction

anchor: Inter-model margins are small enough that engineering considerations can drive the choice
claim_text: Inter-model margins small; engineering considerations can drive model choice

anchor: Tiled contiguously at the serving cadence, these forecasts are the input the following chapters' predictive autoscaling experiments consume
claim_text: Forecasts tiled contiguously at serving cadence serve as input for predictive autoscaling experiments in following chapters
